$comment: Browser testing method selection. Every threshold here exists for a stated reason and is meant to be tuned. Nothing in engine code hard-codes a number that belongs in this file.

ui_known.label: How well the agent already understands this UI
ui_known.why: An unmapped UI cannot be scripted reliably; you must look at it first.

repeatability.label: How often this exact scenario will need re-running
repeatability.why: Repetition is what pays back the cost of writing a script.

determinism_required.label: Whether the answer must be identical run to run
determinism_required.why: Agent-driven exploration is not reproducible; a gate cannot depend on it.

exploratory_value.label: Expected value of open-ended poking around
exploratory_value.why: High when requirements are vague or behaviour is unknown.

ci_suitability.label: Whether this must run unattended in CI
ci_suitability.why: CI needs a deterministic, headless, exit-code-producing artefact.

business_criticality.label: Cost of this flow being broken in production

assertion_complexity.label: Precision of the checks required
assertion_complexity.why: Exact numeric/DOM/network assertions are a script's strength.

maintenance_cost_tolerance.label: Team's appetite for maintaining another test file
maintenance_cost_tolerance.why: Low tolerance argues against adding brittle scripts.

existing_automation.label: How much of this is already covered by existing browser tests

environment_stability.label: How stable the target environment is
environment_stability.why: An unstable target makes a deterministic script fail for the wrong reason.

evidence_requirements.label: Need for trace / video / screenshot artefacts

tool_reliability.label: Observed reliability of the automation tooling here

network_mocking_required.label: Need to intercept or stub network traffic
network_mocking_required.why: Route interception is a deterministic-script capability.

playwright-mcp.label: A. Agent-driven exploratory browser session (Playwright MCP or equivalent)

playwright-script.label: B. Deterministic Playwright (or equivalent) script committed to the repo

existing-tests.label: C. Run the browser tests the repository already has

hybrid.label: D. Explore first, then convert the stable path into a deterministic script

existing-other-tooling.label: E. Use the browser automation stack the repository already standardised on (Cypress, Selenium, WebdriverIO, ...)

hybrid_trigger.$comment: When the UI is poorly understood AND the scenario will be re-run often, exploring and then automating beats either pure approach. Below these values the extra step is not worth it.

existing_first.$comment: If existing automation already covers this well, running it is nearly always the cheapest reliable evidence. Do that before writing anything new.

ambiguity_gate.$comment: Below this score the engine will not commit to a method and escalates instead -- guessing here produces confidently wrong browser strategy.

script_conversion.$comment: Post-exploration rule: when should an exploratory finding become a committed test? See test-automation-lifecycle in the browser-testing skill.

hard_rules.because: A CI gate must be reproducible and produce an exit code. An agent-driven session is neither.
Writing selectors for a UI nobody has looked at produces brittle tests that encode guesses. Explore first.
Open-ended agent interaction with production can trigger real side effects. Requires explicit user authorisation to override.
